records.summary: Build a maintained Chrome and Firefox extension for tracing SAML requests, with optional paid team features. The proposed successor would explain configuration mistakes and support redacted exports, but competitors already offer those features for free.
records.how_money: Optional paid team features were proposed; no verified pricing or revenue.
records.customer: Developers troubleshooting SAML and single sign-on.
records.market: Browser extension market; Chrome and Firefox.

revenue_claims.claim: A developer post reported 27,000+ users for SAML Request Tracer; revenue and paying-user count were not provided or verified.

records.paid_demand: No verified paid buyers or revenue were found. The reported AppBox subscriptions are self-reported and not specific evidence of paying users for this extension.

competitors.name: SAML-tracer (SimpleSAMLphp)
competitors.note: 400,000 Chrome users; updated 2026-08-20. Firefox listing reported 21,442 users and an update on 2026-07-30.

competitors.name: Awesome SAML Tracer
competitors.note: First GitHub commit 2026-05-11; Chrome-Stats creation date 2026-05-19.

competitors.name: SAML Debugger by ClavionX
competitors.note: Product Hunt says launched in 2026, around July; offers explanations of configuration mistakes and redacted diagnostics.

competitors.name: SSO Tracer: SAML & OIDC Debugger (Ninjalabs)
competitors.note: Firefox extension; first version 0.3.0 dated 2026-02-15.

competitors.name: Entra Auth Tracer
competitors.note: Chrome-Stats creation date 2026-04-07.

competitors.name: SAML Chrome Panel
competitors.note: Older comparable tool.

competitors.name: SAMLScope
competitors.note: Product existence and launch are unverified.

competitors.name: samltracer.com “SAML Tracer”
competitors.note: Site returned HTTP 402; store listing appears removed.

rounds.plain: The lead was a successor to a removed SAML tracing extension. The source reports user adoption and subscription monetization among affected extensions, but no verified product revenue.
The initial check found only one verified competing launch in six months, so the two-launch copy-speed threshold was not evidenced.

K2 means at least two competing launches in six months; Awesome SAML Tracer and ClavionX meet that threshold. The proposed diagnostic and redacted-handoff wedge is already free, so the source finds no evident moat (K0: too weak to take 3+ months to copy).

risks: Every live competitor found is free and no verified willingness to pay was found.
The browser-store distribution channel has platform policy and removal risk.
A paid team-sync product would require security review and support; workload under 5 hours/week is unproven.
records.moat: No evident wedge: ClavionX offers diagnostic explanations and redacted exports for free, and SSO Tracer covers some related features. A diagnostic rules engine with safe team handoffs was proposed but is not differentiated in the sources.

hours.value: Could plausibly stay under 5 hours a week for a local-only extension; paid team-sync workload is unproven.
hours.note: The source labels owner hours unverified and the local-only figure as plausible.

records.next_steps: None recommended; the lead was killed. The source says revisiting would mean a different lead: a paid enterprise IdP-diagnostics product with a sales motion.

records.summary: Build a maintained browser extension for developers to test and inspect XPath expressions, with a possible paid tier for saved test suites or team sharing. Google Chrome DevTools already evaluates XPath with $x() and returns matching page elements.
records.how_money: A paid tier for saved test suites or team sharing was proposed; no verified price or revenue for this product.
records.customer: Developers testing or inspecting XPath selectors.
records.market: Chrome browser extension market; geography not specified.

revenue_claims.claim: The original developer reported 20,000+ users; this is not verified active-user or buyer data.
SelectorsHub's vendor license page states Pro is $2.50/month; this is a posted price, not evidence of sales or revenue.

records.paid_demand: No verified product-specific payment count or revenue was found. The original developer said users included paid subscribers, but payer count and revenue are unverified; SelectorsHub posts a Pro price of $2.50/month.

competitors.name: Chrome DevTools $x()
competitors.note: Evaluates XPath and returns matching page elements.

competitors.price: Pro stated as $2.50/month; current checkout price unverified
competitors.note: About 400,000 users in the cited evidence; offers saved values and team account management.

competitors.name: XPath Helper 2.0
competitors.note: 10,000 users and 4.4/11 reported in the kill-check.

competitors.note: 6,000 users reported; listing does not disclose a paid tier.

competitors.name: XPath Selector
competitors.note: 5,000 users reported; listing does not disclose a paid tier.

competitors.name: XPath Tester (developerext7)
competitors.note: Created 2026-06-17; includes local History and Saved features.

competitors.name: Selector Forge
competitors.price: Free tier of 200 selectors per month; paid Intuned plan price unverified
competitors.note: Launched 2026-06-19; generates CSS/XPath selectors and is open source.

competitors.name: CSS Selector & XPath Finder
competitors.note: Offers team syncing and shareable browser artifacts.

rounds.plain: K3 means a platform owner or partner already serves the need. Chrome DevTools' bundled $x() console function handles XPath testing and inspection.
Chrome DevTools covers the core XPath testing need. Saved suites and team sharing also have comparable features in existing tools, while paid demand for this product remains unverified.

risks: Chrome DevTools serves the core testing and inspection need for free.
The original extension's reported user base does not establish revenue or paid conversion.
The original listing was removed; the specific removal cause is unverified, creating store dependence risk.
Owner hours of 4–7 hours/week once stable are an estimate and do not assure the <=5-hour constraint.
records.moat: No strong moat identified. Team-shared suites, history, and integrations could help, but the source says their value is unproven and similar features exist in SelectorsHub and other tools.

hours.value: 4–7 hours/week once stable; 10–20 hours/week during launch and early support
hours.note: Estimated in the source; the <=5-hour constraint is not assured.

records.next_steps: The source suggests a one-day, $0 review-code check for recent explicit requests for reusable suites, team sharing, or paid workflows. Use a pre-set gate such as five independent, recent requests before building; this screens for pain, not willingness to pay.

records.how_money: A paid tier for multiple lists or integrations was proposed; the product's price and paid-plan details are unverified.
records.customer: People who want tasks in a browser new-tab page.
records.market: Chrome browser extension market; geography not specified.

records.paid_demand: No verified product-specific payment count or revenue was found. AppBox said a significant share of affected extensions' users were paying subscribers but did not attribute a count or revenue to New Tab Tasks.

competitors.note: Developer said it had just been published on June 12; store listing later showed 80 users and 7 ratings.

competitors.name: To-do list Chrome extension
competitors.price: Features free; subscription-based ad removal mentioned, price not stated
competitors.note: Listing updated Oct 1, 2026; 605 users reported.

rounds.plain: K2 means at least two competing launches in six months; the scoring notes cite TaskTab and ReadyTab. The notes also cite free incumbents and uncertain paid conversion.
The kill-check found one dated competing launch, TaskTab, but did not find a second dated launch or another evidenced kill rule. Payment and subscriber counts remained unverified.

risks: Current paying-user demand and product revenue are unverified.
Free competitors make willingness to pay uncertain.
Google's July 2026 response said it considered the affected extensions individually and believed enforcement was correct; the specific violation for New Tab Tasks was not publicly stated.
Owner hours under 5 hours/week are unverified; cloud sync and integrations add support and maintenance.
records.moat: No strong moat identified. Habit, task history, and integrations could help, but competitors already offer sync, multiple lists, or integrations. Switching costs appear low to moderate unless a distinctive workflow earns daily use.

hours.value: <=5 hours/week constraint cannot be substantiated; launch and early support workload not quantified
hours.note: Source says owner hours are unverified; a local-first, narrow version may reduce service work.

records.next_steps: The source suggests making a clickable mock and opt-in page for the multi-list and sync proposition, using Momentum's published $39.95/year plan as a visible price benchmark. Share only through a permitted public feedback channel and measure voluntary waitlist or paid-tier-interest clicks; this tests stated interest, not purchases or retention.
